description:
In 1900, sponge divers off the Greek island of Antikythera recovered a calcified lump of bronze from an ancient shipwreck. Decades later, 3D CT scans revealed something historians thought impossible: over 30 precision interlocking bronze gears calculating eclipses, planetary orbits, and the lunar cycle—technology 1,400 years ahead of medieval European clockwork.
